feature: Retain already-read local conversation history and page through thumb scrolling
status: source candidate; combined Android and actual native qualification required before release
changes: Recent pages still paint first, but refreshes merge into the loaded window instead of replacing it.
Older pages prepend by stable row identity; latest text wins by version, and LazyColumn keeps the visible keyed message and pixel offset.
Live rows remain enabled while reading older history; neither the former 500-row nor 1MiB cap hides previously loaded rows.
Within four list items of the older edge, upward reading automatically fetches the next eight-turn page without a pagination button.

Failed edge requests retry with one-second to fifteen-second backoff only while the same owner remains at that edge; switching conversation cancels the reading coroutine and generation/scope checks discard obsolete responses.
A recent refresh after a long absence paints immediately, then fills a missing middle interval asynchronously rather than skipping it.
Older and middle requests preserve current thread status, pending questions, outgoing replies and notification read policy.
Latest/retry and ordinary Android backgrounding retain the loaded history. Real memory pressure evicts inactive cache snapshots, not the current visible conversation.
The inactive per-backend/per-thread cache is four whole windows within a 12MiB estimated serialized UTF-16 budget, with no arbitrary age expiry or partially hidden local pages.
tests_added: Older pages retain recently read rows and recent refresh cannot shrink the window.
More than the former 500-row limit remains readable.
Stale older output cannot roll back live text; overlapping pages deduplicate by identity.
Missing middle pages insert in chronological position after immediate cached/recent paint.
Oldest loaded cursor survives recent refresh, middle bridge and reopen; reaching actual beginning clears hasEarlier.
Prefetch excludes latest-follow, Important filter, distant edge, exhausted history and in-flight requests.
Cache eviction is whole-snapshot and backend/thread isolated; normal elapsed minutes do not expire retained history.

qualification.unit_tests: awaiting root's combined build; no competing Gradle launched while release R8 consumes memory
qualification.native_scroll_anchor: awaiting owned synthetic emulator fixture qualification

limits: This first fix retains local history for the living app process and background/resume; it does not add persistent transcript segments across process death.
Inactive oversized or LRU-evicted windows honestly need refetching through automatic scrolling when reopened.
Active loaded history is not arbitrarily cut. Its memory use scales with actual read history; the inactive serialization budget is an estimate, not a physical-device PSS guarantee.
No private reasoning is requested or exposed; the existing public timeline endpoint and authentication remain unchanged.
